source_title: How tf do people walk in bitterly cold weather?
post_title: How tf do people walk in bitterly cold weather?
post_body:
Just a quick question, how tf do people walk anywhere in this bitterly cold weather?
I'm a freshman if you couldn't tell already.     Every time I go outside, I feel so numb even after wearing layers in this cold weather. The wind hits the snow on my face. How tf do you guys even manage? Pls tell me.
Two layers of pants. A good winter coat and layers on top. Not wearing sneakers. A winter hat and gloves if you need your hands. Not much to help your face, tho I do see some girls with scarves
Neck gaiters are a life saver especially with wind. I spend 12 hours a day outside in state college for work!
I always went:
good beanie that covers the ears
Down coat, put my hands in my sleeves, then into my pocket. Tuck shirt into pants for the walk
Thicker sweatpants and long socks
My last year I got goretex water-proof Nike shoes on clearance for like $30 and they were awesome too.
With all that I would never get cold on my mile+ walk to the business building
other than my face. Always bring tissues to blow your nose in class. Nobody likes a sniffler.
Come to Erie. Well show you a good time. We dont even get classes canceled!
Are you not from PA? Wear fleece and wool base layers, with fleece and wool over top, get a gaiter for your face and neck, and sounds like ski goggles might benefit you.
It's WINDY at Penn State because of the way it sits in the valley & the fact there are no other tall buildings for miles around (source: I made it up but I lived in PA for 28 years and I swear state college is the windiest part of it)
A scarf or balaclava for your face is super helpful, too.
A good coat is key, as is reducing skin exposed to the air
Layers, good heavy coat (parka), winter hat, and gloves. Cover your head, hands and ears or you'll risk frostbite in these temps. Don't spend more time outside than you need to. You'll be fine. I'd take a brutal winter over bad heat waves any day.
Someone from Miami
Flashback to winter of 82. Minus 50-something wind chill. Class in McAllister not cancelled. Walked a mile each way. (See Freezer Bowl football game for reference: San Diego at Cincinnati.) Borrowed roommates ROTC gear. Brutal!
You can wear a covid mask on your face. Its a game changer to keep your skin warm.
Keeping your warm air around your body is the name of the game.
Some of the biggest game changers I've gotten were a balaclava, fleece lined pants, and heated gloves. If you want a really hardcore suggestion, insulated work bibs, you'll get a lifetime out of them with gentle use or a decade or two with abuse.
It should also go without saying: warm socks. Especially if you have shoes with any sort of ventilation.
Cold is 90% psychological, don't fight the cold, embrace it.
Hot hands Hand warmers. Buy a value size bag on Amazon. Activate a pack and place one in each of your coat pockets, or one in each glove. Use that warmth for your ears, nose, cheeks. Theyve been lifesavers for me many, many, times. Keep a few pairs in your car for times youre stuck walking somewhere and not dressed warm enough.
Make sure your ears, fingers, and toes are as insulated as possible. There's really no "fix", you'll just acclimate over time, but if those areas are exposed you'll suffer more.
My personal getup is a good pair of cargo pants that Ive found to work in almost any environment anyway, a pair of work boots in case I have to walk through the snow, three layers on top and gloves (though I do need to get new ones as mine are starting to develop holes and arent holding warmth in so good anymore). If the snow and wind starts attacking you, think of investing in a scarf, mask or (if you really wanna protect your eyes) goggles which came in handy for me a few weeks ago when I had to go out during the snowstorm. Be sure to also follow the advice of the others here and only go out for as long as you need to and not any longer.
Trick question you dont. Either get one of your friends that has a car to drive you, uber, take the bus, or simply take a personal day haha. But I all seriousness like others have said wear double layers (triple if you have to) and thermals. Shoes that are meant for your foot to breathe are your enemy. Boot and thick socks are necessary. Do not cheapen out on gloves either, your still attached fingers will thank you. Also I you dont have one already try to get a thick heavy duty jacket from like the thrift store or something to save money. Cover all areas where your skin is exposed (so no wearing cropped sweatpants with the ankle showing), because if you can see your skin after getting dressed, the wind can too. This is my first real winter also as Im from Alabama, however from getting lots of advice from Northerners/locals, as long as your feet, chest, head, and face are covered up, its will be okay.
Lots of good advice. And this is a worse than normal winter. My best tips are a good hat, scarf/baclava, and good shoes (boots, gortex, winter shoes). And a winter coat, I like coats that are three in one models... layers help.
My other piece of advice. Walk routes through buildings. It might take longer but walking through a classroom building on your way can help. At least mentally it breaks up the walk.
Hang in there.
hermal pants with another layer of pants, thermal shirt with a crewneck or hoodie, two pairs of socks (one normal one fluffy), boots, hand warmers, scarf, winter jacket, always wear the hood or a hat
I make sure my outer layer is highly wind resistant. Then it is a matter a layering and wearing shoes that dont let wind through them. Alternatively you could spring for winter jackets that can handle certain temperatures better. Many people run, walk, ski, and party in these temps. Gear quality and proper dressing are critical. Always protect the ears, hands, and have pants that block wind really well
I'm always hot, so I'm not really feeling the cold until we get below 30. In the single digits I have a good winter coat, a hat, plus my coat's hat (which clips in front of half my face), and gloves. If I am going to be outside for several hours then I get out my winter boots, double layer my pants (thin athletic pants plus jeans), and add another sweater layer. I am also looking at getting a balaclava because I ride an ebike and want to protect my face more.
Always hated the eye burn when its stupid cold and windy. I picked up a pair of tight fitting wraparound sunglasses. Get the amber vision ones and they make things look artificially happy and warm.
Also look up neoprene face masks. I hate scarves and these cover the nose, cheeks, and neck and has holes for breathing so the stuff doesnt get soaking wet then freeze or fog your glasses. I work outside for hours in this nastiness. These things are a game changer.
You first need a good thermal base layer (both top and bottom). The brand Cuddl Duds makes an extra warm version rated for frigid climates. Thats what I bought. You can get them at Target or online. They should be fitted to your skin so cold air cant get under them.
Wear pants or lined leggings over the thermal bottoms and then a good warm sweater or hoodie on the top. Add another fleece shirt under the sweater or hoodie if you get cold quickly or have lower body fat.
Then add a good down fill winter coat (at least a 700 down fil rating). If youre buying alternative down, check the tag and itll tell you what temp its rated for.
If you get a skimpy lightweight coat its not going to keep you warm. Thats a mistake I see a lot of people making. These coats are more expensive, but you can find them for less on eBay. I recommend Patagonia or North Face.
Wear warm socks and boots. If you prefer sneakers, make sure they arent those thin mesh running shoes (like Nike rosche run) those will not keep your feet warm.
Dont forget gloves and a hat!
this winter sucks i'll be honest. my usual layering is:
wool socks that go up to my knees
undershirt
wool leggings
pants (jeans aren't recommended but you can. i do jeans a lot and usually i can survive as long as i have the leggings)
winter coat
scarf (after hat, so i can also cover any parts of my neck/face not covered by my hat)
two hoods from hoodie+coat over hat
i also stuff the long end of the scarf down my coat. it looks stupid but the fact that it's not outside of the coat adds insulation, and i'd rather look stupid than have frostbite. however i also have a handknit scarf made from thick wool so it's a bit bulkier than most scarves. usually when i'm done layering, only my eyes are visible and i can get to class.... relatively okay. good luck out there, stay warm!
